answer: A reputation anchor works like this: every agent must stake coins on a single persistent identity, and that stake is slashed if the identity is caught attesting falsely. New identities start as isolated islands with no trust, so a sybil army of fresh accounts earns nothing until each builds history. A bridge of cross-attestation lets established agents vouch for newcomers, but the voucher’s own stake is at risk, so vouching is rationed. Creating a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand stakes plus the time to build trust, while one honest identity stays cheap.
